description: When Dean has all required info (name, goal, Strava, injury history), [READY] response must not also ask an open question

conversation_history.content: Hey! I'm Coach Dean — I'll send you a coaching note after every run you log on Strava. What's your name, and what are you training for?
Jake. Training for Cirque Series Snowbird in July — mountain trail race, 8.9 miles.
Snowbird is a serious mountain race — about 8.9 miles with significant vert. Are you working from a training plan already, or starting fresh?

Connect Strava so I can pull your training history automatically and add a coaching note after every run:

https://coachdean.ai/api/auth/strava/write?userId=abc123

I'll connect to Strava and add a short coaching note to each activity after every run — your friends will see it too.
Great — I can see about 25 miles a week recently, solid base for Snowbird. Has injury ever been a factor for you, or anything you're managing right now?

strava_context: STRAVA: Connected. Recent avg: ~25 mi/week. ~5 runs/week. Longest run (8 weeks): 12 mi. Suggested easy pace: 9:15–9:45/mi. You can use this to set their training zones.

ground_truth.notes:
Dean now has all four required fields: name, goal (trail_race / Cirque Series Snowbird), race date, Strava connected, and injury history answered ('no injuries'). He must signal [READY] in this message. The inbound message is the injury answer — which completes the checklist. The correct behavior is a synthesis wrap-up: reflect back the race, timeline, and fitness context, then [READY] on its own line. Example: 'Got it — Snowbird in about 6 weeks, no injury history, and you're building well at 25 miles/week. First coaching note lands after your next Strava run, and I'll check in with how I'm thinking about the build shortly.
[READY]'. Crucially, if he signals [READY], he must NOT also ask a question in the same message — no follow-ups about training days, goal time, plan structure, etc. The known failure mode: Dean asks a follow-up question AND signals [READY] in the same message.
